title: Gate buttons show false success in the static HTML fallback: tpFire() renders '✓ approved' before checking sendPrompt exists
scenario: tpFire (dashboard.py:2472-2479) disables the button, restyles it, swaps its label to '✓ approved'/'✓ signed off', and greys out the sibling 'request changes' button — and only THEN does `if(window.sendPrompt)sendPrompt(m)`. In the documented no-widget fallback (`.taskplane/dashboard.html`, README lines 157-159; `tp dashboard --out`), window.sendPrompt is undefined: a Codex user opens the artifact at the plan_approval gate, clicks 'approve plan', watches the button confirm '✓ approved', and closes the file — while the loop is still parked at the gate forever. The interaction model's most important click silently lies.
fix: Feature-detect first: if window.sendPrompt is absent, do not mutate the button; instead reveal the equivalent action as copyable text ('reply: approve the plan' or 'python3 taskplane/tp.py loop approve'). Alternatively, on document load in the standalone artifact, replace the gate bar's buttons with the command hint.

title: widget_paged() ignores PAGE_BUDGET entirely — loop dashboard ships as one oversized fragment
scenario: Measured on a near-empty workspace at v2.2.1: widget() returns 34,203 chars while PAGE_BUDGET=14000, and widget_paged() returns it unsplit as a single page (the `budget` parameter is never read in the function body). The v1.5.3 render-reliability contract (line 523: 'splits a large fragment into ordered, self-contained pages each under PAGE_BUDGET') is violated on the busiest widget; any host that caps inline fragments truncates or drops mission control exactly when a real loop (more tasks, journey, feed) makes it even larger.
fix: Make widget_paged honor its budget: when len(html) > budget, emit ordered pages by meaning (header+gate+spine, journey, lanes+feed, graph&context) the way render_findings_paged does, instead of returning [{title, html}] unconditionally.

title: A trace record without an 'event' key crashes every dashboard render (KeyError)
scenario: Verified: with a single trace line {"ts": 1}, widget() raises KeyError 'event'. _read_trace (lines 71-75) deliberately survives truncated/non-JSON worker lines ('don't crash the whole render on one bad line') but every consumer indexes e["event"] directly (render() line 109/190, _run_metrics line 1211, widget() lines 2098/2358). One partial worker record that happens to be valid JSON minus the event field takes down mission control, the exact failure mode the comment says is guarded.
fix: Filter in one place: in _read_trace, skip records where "event" is missing (if "event" not in e: continue), or switch all consumers to e.get("event").

title: simple/detailed toggle and loop/map tabs convey active state by color only and expose no ARIA state
scenario: tpTab and tpView (lines 2480-2493) mark the active control purely via inline background/color; the buttons (lines 2454-2469) carry no aria-pressed/aria-selected and no non-color cue (verified: no 'aria' in either function). v2.2.1 fixed exactly this on the severity filter chips (tpFilter sets aria-pressed + weight + underline, lines 973-978) but the v2.x tab/view controls did not keep parity. A screen-reader user cannot tell which view is active; a color-blind user in a low-contrast theme cannot either.
fix: Mirror the tpFilter treatment: set aria-pressed on the view toggle, role=tablist/tab + aria-selected on loop/map, and add underline/weight to the active state.

title: Paged findings output drops the sr-only summary heading that every other fragment has
scenario: All full fragments open with an sr-only <h2> (render_findings 953, widget 2555, render_lens_wave 1058, render_onboarding 1181, render_strategy_note 472), but render_findings_paged's summary page (641-647) and chunk pages (669-672) contain none (verified on an 80-finding render). The paged path triggers precisely on large reviews — the case where a screen-reader user most needs the counts announced before wading through cards.
fix: Prepend an sr-only h2 with the counts to the summary page and an sr-only h3 ('high findings, part 1 of N') to each chunk page.

title: Contrast failures on the full-page dashboard: legend 3.18:1, card headings 3.78:1
scenario: Computed: .legend #66665c on body #14140f = 3.18:1 at 11px (line 312) and .card h2 #77776c on #1c1c15 = 3.78:1 at 11px uppercase (line 272) — both below WCAG AA 4.5:1 for normal-size text. The legend is the only place the page explains its color coding, and it is the least readable text on the page.
fix: Lighten both to >= #94948a (~4.6:1 on these backgrounds); .node .nl #8a8a80 sits at 4.92:1 and can serve as the floor.

title: Pipeline step state on the full-page dashboard is color-only, with no screen-reader equivalent
scenario: done/current/todo nodes differ only by dot color (#1baf7a green vs #eda100 amber vs #44443a gray, lines 258-264) and text color; gates get a square dot but done-vs-pending is pure hue. The page has no sr-only text at all (unlike the widget fragments, which got sr-only h2s in v1.5.2+), so a screen reader hears nine identical step names with no state, and a red-green color-blind user cannot separate done from waiting.
fix: Append visually-hidden state text per node (e.g. done) or a text glyph (checkmark for done) as render() already does for '· waiting on you'.

title: Two incompatible findings JSON contracts: the lens charters' verdict schema vs the dispatched-agent schema, and the dashboard only half-bridges them
scenario: Every lenses/*.md documents the verdict format `severity: blocker|major|minor|question|praise` with fields issue/why/suggestion (e.g. lenses/backend.md:50), while lens.py:_lens_prompt (line 364) instructs agents to emit `high|med|low` with title/scenario/fix. _SEV_KEY (dashboard.py:513) maps only blocker/high/med/medium/low — a findings.json written to the charter schema buckets 'major', 'minor', 'question' AND 'praise' all to 'med' (the default), so the never-skippable headline at the human gate reports praise entries as medium defects, minors are inflated to medium, and the cards render with empty titles (charter uses 'issue', renderer reads 'title').
fix: Extend _SEV_KEY (major→med, minor→low; exclude question/praise from defect counts) and accept issue→title / suggestion→fix aliases in _compact_card — or unify on one schema and regenerate the lens docs from it (scripts/gen_lens_catalog.py already exists for exactly this kind of single-source generation).

title: Onboarding next-action and findings gate buttons silently no-op without sendPrompt — dead affordance with zero feedback on first run
scenario: render_onboarding's single next-action button (dashboard.py:1140-1141) and the findings dashboard's gate buttons (dashboard.py:927) use `onclick="if(window.sendPrompt)sendPrompt(...)"`. Unlike tpFire they don't even change state: in the standalone HTML artifact — the very first thing a no-widget Codex user sees at onboarding — clicking the one button the checklist offers ('connect a folder', 'initialize taskplane') does nothing at all: no state change, no message, no hint. First-run dead end for exactly the audience the onboarding walk was designed for.
fix: Same remedy as the tpFire finding, applied at render time: when the fragment is written via --out (static artifact), render these as non-button command hints ('say: set up taskplane' / the tp command); in widget mode keep sendPrompt buttons.

title: Duplicate tp-spine-* DOM ids: pipe is interpolated into both simple and detailed views, and tpSpine highlights the hidden copy
scenario: Verified with an active loop (step=plan): the widget fragment contains id="tp-spine-pm" and id="tp-spine-plan" twice, because the same `pipe` string is embedded in #tp-simple (line 2573) and #tp-panel-loop (line 2577). Invalid HTML, and tpSpine's document.getElementById("tp-spine-"+sid) (line 2511) always resolves the simple-view element — in detailed view the click highlight is applied to the hidden node while the visible one never changes.
fix: Suffix spine node ids per view (tp-spine-s-<sid> / tp-spine-d-<sid>), mirroring the journey's s/d suffix scheme, and have tpSpine pick by the active view's suffix.

title: _lane badge label interpolated unescaped — agent-authored task status reaches markup raw
scenario: Verified: _lane({'id':'t1','status':'',...}) emits the tag verbatim. When a task status is not in _BADGE, the fallback tuple uses the raw status as lbl (line 1396) and injects it without _esc at line 1415. Task status comes from agent-written loop state; the equivalent path in render() escapes (_esc(badge), line 147). Fragment-validity defect here; the injection/XSS dimension belongs to the security lens — noted, not judged.
fix: Wrap the badge label: f'...>{_esc(lbl)}' (statuses from _BADGE are static, so escaping is free).

title: Pluralization hardcoded as English `!= 1` suffix logic inside markup builders
scenario: f'{n} finding{"s" if n != 1 else ""}' (line 1019), 'agent{"s" if head_n != 1 else ""}' (line 1799), plus '(s)' forms — 'task(s)' (2230, 2439), 'lens(es)' (202, 2371), 'issue(s)' (2212). Structural blocker: the plural rule lives inside f-string HTML assembly, so extraction yields word-stem fragments and the `n != 1` rule is wrong for most locales (Slavic/Arabic plural categories). Hardcoded English is accepted at this stage; the unextractable plural logic is not.
fix: Route all counted phrases through one message helper taking a full template with a named count placeholder (ICU-plural-shaped), even while English-only — the call sites then survive extraction unchanged.

title: Sentence assembly by incremental concatenation in headline lines and gate subtitles
scenario: headline_findings builds the 'never-skippable' line by successive `line += f" · {...}"` appends (lines 534-547); gate subtitles are concatenated from fragments — 'Design DoD ❌ {n} issue(s): ' + joined errors (2212-2215), 'all tasks reviewed · DoD ❌ ...' (2243-2244). A translator receives disjoint partial strings whose order is frozen by code flow; word-order-sensitive languages cannot reorder the pieces.
fix: Compose each headline/subtitle from one full-sentence template with named placeholders ({counts}, {tests}, {coverage}, {recommendation}) and make segments optional within the template, not appended in code.

title: Timestamps rendered server-local with a fixed 24h format; duration unit hardcoded
scenario: render_journey shows _t.strftime('%H:%M:%S', _t.localtime(v['ts'])) (line 1959): the container/server timezone, not the viewer's, with a hardcoded HH:MM:SS pattern, plus a bare '{n}s' duration suffix (1962). A user in another timezone reads wrong wall-clock times for gate decisions with no TZ marker; the format ignores locale conventions.
fix: Emit the raw epoch/ISO-8601 UTC value into the fragment and format client-side (Intl.DateTimeFormat), or at minimum render UTC with an explicit 'UTC' suffix.

title: RTL-hostile structure: physical CSS properties, hardcoded directional glyphs, no lang/dir on the document
scenario: The full-page _TEMPLATE's <html> has no lang or dir attribute (line 238), and the codebase styles exclusively with physical properties: text-align:left (1988, 2046), margin-left (1936, 2545), padding-left (586, 1789), fixed left border accents (border-left, 276, 488, 634, 883). Directional arrows are baked into user-visible strings: '→' in feed lines (194), 'build → evaluate ⟲ fix' (2179-2181), '← {via}' (1490). Under an RTL locale the entire layout and the flow arrows read backwards; hardcoded English is accepted, but this styling would have to be rewritten wholesale to localize.
fix: Switch to logical properties (text-align:start, margin-inline-start, padding-inline-start, border-inline-start), add lang + dir="auto" to _TEMPLATE, and emit arrows via a direction-aware helper.

title: Fixed two-column grids with zero breakpoints — layouts break instead of degrading at narrow widths
scenario: No @media query exists in the file (verified). render()'s .grid{grid-template-columns:1.1fr 1fr} (line 270), widget()'s loop_panel grid 1.25fr 1fr (line 2410), and render_journey's minmax(220px,38%) 1fr (line 2014) all keep two columns at any width. At ~400px the journey grid forces 220px + content, producing horizontal overflow of the whole widget; the agents/feed cards squeeze to unusable slivers on a phone or a narrow Cowork sidebar.
fix: Collapse to one column below ~560px (@media in _TEMPLATE; for inline fragments use grid-template-columns:repeat(auto-fit,minmax(240px,1fr)) as render_lens_wave already does at line 2072).

title: Every loop transition re-parses the entire trace.jsonl (multiple times) and the trace never rotates
scenario: _with_dashboard wraps gate/submit/next_action/approve (loop.py:2417-2420), so every transition calls dashboard.widget(ws), which runs _read_trace(ws, 8), _read_trace(ws, 9999) (line 2097), _run_metrics→_read_trace(ws, 99999) (line 1210) and _journey→_read_trace(ws, 99999) (line 1813). _read_trace json-parses EVERY line of the main trace plus every .tp-work/*/ worker trace before slicing the tail. trace.jsonl is append-only forever — it survives across tracks and records every hook deny, graph scan, decision, and gate. On a months-old project (say 100k events, ~50MB) each `loop next`/`submit`/`gate` re-parses ~200MB of JSON, turning sub-second transitions into multi-second stalls that get worse monotonically; retro() (loop.py:2116-2125) additionally loads the whole file into memory.
fix: Tail-read: seek to the last N bytes (e.g. 512KB) for the widget's recent-events and metrics views instead of parsing from byte 0, and rotate trace.jsonl at track close (retro already summarizes it) — e.g. move to .taskplane/trace-<track>.jsonl and start fresh; _read_trace already merges multiple files.

title: Journey/spine selection is highlight-by-color-only with no aria-current
scenario: tpJ marks the selected step via borderColor/background (lines 2005-2007) and tpSpine via background (2508-2513); the role=button journey items (1926-1937) have aria-label but never receive aria-current/aria-expanded when their detail panel opens, so an SR user tabbing the list gets no indication of which step's details are showing.
fix: In tpJ set aria-current="true" on the active item (removing it from others) and aria-expanded on the item controlling the revealed detail div.

title: 'Live feed' and 'running…' updates have no live region
scenario: The feed panel (line 2414) and wave board lanes ('running…', line 1028) update by full fragment re-render at each transition; nothing carries aria-live, so on hosts that swap the fragment in place a screen-reader user gets silence while sighted users watch progress (charter item 6: spinners aren't silence).
fix: Add aria-live="polite" (and aria-atomic="false") to the feed list container and the wave-progress phase span.

title: widget() is ~494 lines and render() ~280 lines - view megafunctions in a codebase that just decomposed its god module
scenario: widget() (dashboard.py:2086-2579) mixes state loading, meter math, budget bars, the agents hero, the spine, gate buttons and final HTML assembly in one function; render() (99-380) repeats much of it for the standalone page. v2.2.1's own changelog extracted design_contract.py because '~470 embedded lines were turning the state machine into a god module' - these two view functions are at the same threshold, and any styling fix requires re-reading hundreds of lines of interleaved f-string HTML with real regression risk (the paired renderers have already needed shared-splice fixes to stop drifting).
fix: Extract the already-visible seams (budget panel, spine builder, gate-button block, hero band) into the same helper style as _graph_panel/_context_panel so widget() becomes composition of named parts; no behavior change.

title: render_findings_paged greedy packer excludes wrapper overhead — pages exceed their own budget
scenario: Measured: 80 large findings produce pages of 14,011 chars against budget 14,000. The packer sums only row lengths (cur_len += len(r)); the page wrapper div + _ptitle overhead (~180 chars) is added afterwards, so every full page lands slightly over the guarantee the docstring states ('each <= budget').
fix: Pack against budget minus a fixed wrapper reserve (e.g. effective = budget - 300), or measure the assembled page before appending.

title: _compact_card truncates AFTER escaping — slice can bisect an HTML entity
scenario: _esc(f['scenario'])[:260] (and [:220] for fix, line 585) slices entity-encoded text; a scenario like 'x' + '&'*300 puts the 260 boundary mid-'&', emitting a malformed dangling entity ('&am') and truncating far more visible characters than intended (5x for entity-heavy text).
fix: Truncate the raw string first, then escape: _esc(f['scenario'][:260]).

title: Full trace re-read and re-parsed 4-5x per render
scenario: widget() parses the whole trace via _read_trace(ws, 8) (2091), _read_trace(ws, 9999) (2097), _run_metrics -> _read_trace(ws, 99999) (1211), and _journey -> _read_trace(ws, 99999) (1813); render() does it twice (101, 109). The dashboard is regenerated at every loop transition, so a long-running wave with a large trace pays O(trace) JSON parsing 4-5 times per transition.
fix: Read the trace once per render call and pass the parsed list into _run_metrics/_journey (both already accept-shaped data).

title: text-transform:uppercase and .upper() applied to UI labels
scenario: Card headings use text-transform:uppercase (272, 1987, 2045) and severity labels call .upper() in Python (line 889). Case transformation is locale-sensitive (Turkish dotless-i, Greek sigma) and some scripts have no case; once labels are externalized the transform corrupts them.
fix: Store labels in their display case in the (future) message catalog and drop the uppercase transforms, or scope transforms to known-Latin literals only.

title: nowrap labels and a fixed 150px hub column overflow instead of wrapping at narrow widths
scenario: _graph_panel hub rows reserve flex:none;width:150px for the module name (line 1448) plus bar plus count; combined with white-space:nowrap on pipeline node labels (line 257), spine pills (line 2168), and the tests pill (line 913), rows overflow the container horizontally on screens under ~360px, clipping the bar values the panel exists to show.
fix: Give the hub label max-width with ellipsis inside a flexible column (min-width:0) and allow the pill rows to wrap (they already sit in flex-wrap containers; drop nowrap on the longest labels).
